evidence: In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry and mass spectrometry were applied to demonstrate the ALD self-limiting behavior and to gain insight into the surface reactions during the precursor and co-reactant exposures, respectively. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to probe the thickness of the films along individual InP nanowires. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) was used to probe the chemical composition along the InP nanowires. Elastic recoil detection (ERD) and Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy (RBS) were carried out to determine the composition and mass density of the films. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra were recorded. The growth per super-cycle was measured by profilometry, spectrophotometry, transmission electron microscopy or spectroscopic ellipsometry. Film composition was determined by Rutherford backscattering spectrometry and/or elastic recoil detection, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance and/or x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy measurements. The crystallinity of the AlxPOy layers was investigated using a Philips X'Pert MPD diffractometer. A Pfeiffer Vacuum mass spectrometer was connected to the deposition chamber. The results of the saturation behavior of the AlxPOy supercycle are presented in Fig. 2. The growth per super-cycle and [P]:[Al] ratio for a substrate temperature of 150 °C. The [P]:[Al] ratio gives an indication on the phosphorus incorporation in the films. The combination of TEM and EDX gives insight into the conformality of the AlxPOy films. The mass density of ALD Al2O3 films is found to be ~ 2.8 g· cm-3. The as-deposited aluminum phosphate films were also characterized by XRD and where found to be amorphous for the whole temperature range of 25 to 300 °C. The optical constants of the AlxPOy films deposited at different temperatures were evaluated using ex-situ VASE measurements. The refractive index versus [P]:[Al] ratio for films deposited using substrate temperatures from 25 -300 °C and an 1:1 cycle ratio. The refractive index and [P]:[Al] ratio were determined from SE and the XPS analysis, respectively. The inset shows refractive index of films from 190 – 1000 nm determined by ex-situ VASE for films deposited at 150 °C using a 1:1 and 3:1 cycle ratio.
